content.intro: In this lesson, focus on static theme variables and css variable output and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Static Theme Variables and CSS Variable Output helps a team reuse visual decisions without losing flexibility for real application interfaces.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Understanding used-variable generation; Static theme generation; Accessing theme variables from CSS; Using tokens in inline styles; Handling variables that do not map to utilities. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to static theme variables and css variable output, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to static theme variables and css variable output.

troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying static theme variables and css variable output without checking generated styles or browser behavior.

Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Static Theme Variables and CSS Variable Output is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
